tech.summary: You've been there: code's ready to ship, everyone's excited—then someone spots a vulnerability. Suddenly it's an all-hands emergency and time to cancel your evening plans. Microsoft Azure bakes security in from the start. Microsoft Defender for Cloud helps keep your apps and code protected throughout the development lifecycle. Less last-minute surprises, more peace of mind. Ship fast. Ship safely. Do both at the same time. Build with built-in security →

tech.title: Apple's Claris Testing 'Harbor' App for Local AI on Macs
tech.summary: Harbor is an app currently being tested by Apple's Claris subsidiary that turns Apple Silicon Macs into private AI servers. It supports connecting multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory and enable larger models with higher concurrency. Harbor is in early access and not publicly available. There was an App Store listing, but it has now been removed, so it isn't clear whether the app will be free. The sign-up page for the app asks for a company name, suggesting a business focus.

tech.title: Amazon's Ring unveils flying drone and robot to patrol homes and businesses
tech.summary: The Ring Drone Cam is a security camera that can fly from room to room to investigate suspicious activity. For $250, the drone can fly up to eight minutes at a time before autonomously returning to its charging dock. The Ring Rover Cam is a $1,000 device with a display and an extendable periscope camera mounted on a two-wheeled base. The Ring Drone Cam will ship in the US on January 27 (pending approval from the FCC), and the Ring Rover Cam will start shipping on December 16.

tech.title: ‘Flying cars' could launch in China next summer, maker of two-seat model says
tech.summary: XPeng's $300,000 low-altitude flying car will be ready for use in the second half of 2027. About the size of a Fiat 500, the vehicle can fly using six drone-like battery-powered propellers. It can be steered using a joystick or fly autonomously to a programmed destination. The price tag includes a six-wheeled van for transporting the vehicle. The flying car has a flight range of 30 kilometers, but XPeng says this will soon be doubled.

tech.title: Starlink Mini 2 Has a Swappable Battery, But It Costs Way More Than Expected
tech.summary: The Starlink Mini 2 is the first Starlink dish to support the company's swappable battery, which lasts up to 4.5 hours. SpaceX is asking early adopters to pay $999 to own it. That fee includes a full year of Starlink Roam Unlimited, which is usually valued at $2,100. Shipments are estimated to begin in mid-December.

tech.title: Stop your AI agents from going rogue
tech.summary: Ask an email agent to summarize your inbox, and it reads the message an attacker wrote to look like an instruction. That's how indirect prompt injection turns a helpful agent into a damaging tool call. Gray Swan CPO, Spencer Whitman, shows how to secure production agents with three layers: red-teaming, behavior enforcement and deterministic controls. Save your seat ->

tech.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
tech.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon features frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning. It is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for Business for all paying developers and enterprises. It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search.

tech.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0: The web platform expertise your coding agent is missing
tech.summary: The Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into coding agents. The stable release of the guidance includes a new modernization workflow, an expanded guide database, deeper human expert review for every guide, and full evaluation coverage across all of the guides. Firefox and Edge have joined Chrome to support Modern Web Guidance to improve cross-browser compatibility and contribute to the project. The project aims to ensure that anyone coding with agents can take full advantage of the power and capabilities of the modern web platform.

tech.title: Anthropic to Seek $1.3 Trillion Valuation in IPO
tech.summary: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at a range of $70 to $78 a share in its initial public offering, which is expected to start trading on Thursday of next week. The company expects to raise an additional $26 billion from big investors, including Google and AMD. Some Anthropic executives and founding members plan to sell around 23.6 million shares in the offering. At the planned valuation, Anthropic's IPO won't top SpaceX's record-breaking offering in June.

tech.title: Q3.5 Timelines Update: Looks Like the Intelligence Explosion Will Happen in 2027 After All
tech.summary: A Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) is predicted to arrive at some point in 2027, assuming there is no substantial deliberate slowdown in development. AIs that can automate all white-collar work are predicted to arrive before 2028. Companies are currently not on track to align an SAR, and using a misaligned SAR to do recursive self-improvement will have negative consequences. China will probably be able to steal the training recipe and maybe even the model weights if an SAR is trained in the near future.

tech.summary: Nexus picks the best model for each turn inside your existing tools. At max effort it scored 89.3% vs. 86.8% for Claude Opus 5.5 at 17% lower cost. 👉 Try Nexus

tech.summary: The super network feature is now rolling out to Pixel 9 and above devices with eSIMs.

tech.summary: Reddit Reviews is rolling out to all users in the US on iOS, Android, and the web.

webdev.title: Dev Workshop: Identify traffic from AI agents, bots, and humans in one hour
webdev.summary: Three visitors walk into your checkout page: a real customer, a bot script, and Meta's Muse making a purchase on a customer's behalf. If you're blocking everyone, the joke's on you. But how do you tell them apart? On Nov 17 , Fingerprint's Keshia Rose builds a server-side policy layer live, then sends all three at it. webdev.title: The Codebase Rewrite Is Back
webdev.summary: AI is changing rewrite economics because existing applications give agents a specification to reproduce, making previously expensive migrations and backlog work worth reconsidering. Examples from GitHub, Shopify, and Bun show faster rewrites, but hidden behavior and regressions make end-to-end tests, benchmarks, and reversible rollouts essential.

webdev.title: MCP or CLI? Yes
webdev.summary: Sentry is combining its CLI and MCP server so agents can share CLI authentication while retaining native tool discovery. The CLI handles filesystem-heavy work such as searching session replay logs, while MCP exposes discoverable tools, though inconsistent client support still limits richer integrations.

webdev.title: Building a Microapp Inside a Plugin: Architecture and Tradeoffs
webdev.summary: Carta's microapps fetch data through MCP once at launch, then run a local React application against a snapshot with deterministic, auditable business logic. A no-build shell lets users customize the code while updates preserve their data, but the architecture trades real-time refreshes and live collaboration for local ownership and responsive analysis.

webdev.title: AI Usage Generates a Fragile Codebase
webdev.summary: Heavy reliance on AI coding can produce shallow tests, unnecessary abstractions, weaker human understanding, and pull requests that arrive faster than reviewers can inspect them. These habits lead to more incidents, slower recovery, and user-facing failures that coverage metrics miss.

webdev.title: Life on Claude Nine
webdev.summary: This speculative short story follows an engineer whose Claude-powered automations grow from handling email into systems he can no longer understand or control. It explores how productivity gains, compulsive building, and increasingly automatic approvals can turn human oversight into a formality.

webdev.title: Domains, hosting, and email. Built into your workflow.
webdev.summary: Deploy Node.js apps through GoDaddy's APIs or the gddy CLI. Then use the APIs to register domains, configure DNS, and set up professional email in one connected workflow. Access developer pricing on eligible domain registrations. → Explore APIs → See domain pricing

webdev.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0
webdev.summary: Modern Web Guidance packages browser expertise and compatibility data as skills for coding agents, with expert-reviewed guidance on accessibility, performance, security, and modern platform features. Version 1.0 adds a static-analysis modernization workflow, public evaluations, and contributions from Firefox and Edge alongside Chrome.

webdev.title: billion-context
webdev.summary: billion-context sits between coding agents and model APIs to compress conversation history into layered summaries while preserving the ability to restore details. It exposes compression, decompression, search, and context-status tools, aiming to keep long sessions within smaller context windows without repeatedly discarding history.

webdev.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Is Now Available
webdev.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon targets complex coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and scientific reasoning with longer reasoning and verification loops than Argon. It is available to paying API users at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, alongside a rollout to Google AI Ultra subscribers.

webdev.title: chrome-capture
webdev.summary: Chrome's new screen recording protocol command replaces a decade-old pipeline of JPEG frames piped to ffmpeg with AV1 MP4s encoded directly from the compositor at 60 to 120fps and up to 2160p, with optional tab audio. In benchmarks against Playwright's recordVideo, stopping a recording took 17 ms instead of 3.8 s, and the overall test finished about 10 seconds sooner, with far less WebSocket traffic. It works with Playwright, Puppeteer, or raw CDP and includes a test fixture, making it relevant to anyone recording browser tests or demos.

webdev.title: The Era of Fully Autonomous Companies
webdev.summary: Agent-managed companies need persistent shared state, coordination, code, payment access, and concrete goals that can be checked against real business results. Rapid growth is predicted in autonomous businesses, but demand generation, bot defenses, identity requirements, and human sales cycles remain obstacles.

webdev.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code
webdev.summary: AlphaProof Code combines human-reviewed specifications with AI agents that generate Lean proofs for key security properties of Signal's compiled cryptographic code. DeepMind reports completing the verification in four weeks with over six million lines of Lean. The system also proved two deliberately reintroduced historical bugs insecure.

webdev.title: Deploy an AI Agent with a Feedback Loop Today on Chalk
webdev.summary: Build with fresh data and any model. Evaluate against your dataset. Deploy with guardrails. Improve by comparing runs side by side. All in one project, with nothing to provision. Try Chalk now.

webdev.title: The Secret of the MacBook's Glowing Apple
webdev.summary: A teardown found a separate four-LED strip behind the glowing logo.

webdev.title: Understanding React Internals
webdev.summary: An introduction to React's scheduler that explains why hooks work and previews a series on lanes, hydration, server serialization, and the render and commit phases.

webdev.title: Swarm Riders and Swarm-Native Companies
webdev.summary: Managing productive agent swarms is framed as a distinct skill centered on reward functions, evaluations, and turning ambiguous work into verifiable tasks.

webdev.title: Get Started with MCP Apps
webdev.summary: Build interactive interfaces inside Claude with the MCP Apps SDK.

webdev.title: An Open Field Guide to Inference Engineering
webdev.summary: This practical guide maps platform engineering skills onto production inference, covering GPU memory, KV caches, serving engines, observability, costs, and operational lessons from real deployments.

devops.title: When your AI agent sends the wrong email, it's already too late to scope the key
devops.summary: 18% of teams had an AI agent send a wrong email last quarter, per Nylas's new survey. Nylas IAM gives each agent its own key, scoped to one mailbox if you want. Try to send on a read-only key and the Nylas gateway refuses it before Google or Microsoft ever sees the request. Every call gets logged, refusals included. Included on every plan. See how Nylas IAM works →

devops.title: Now generally available: GKE dynamic slicing for higher resilience, and efficiency for TPUs
devops.summary: Google Kubernetes Engine dynamic slicing is now generally available for TPUs. It separates slice formation from nodepool provisioning, cutting AI workload startup times by up to 5x and recovery times by 4.5x.

devops.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes: Hardware-enforced workload isolation on Amazon EKS
devops.summary: AWS Nitro Sandboxes provides hardware-enforced workload isolation for Amazon EKS pods by running each one inside its own lightweight virtual machine. The feature allows users to enable strong security boundaries with a single line in the pod spec without changing container images or deployment pipelines. It offers isolated mode for standard protection and confidential mode for cryptographic attestation.

devops.title: See what your Argo CD applications cost
devops.summary: Cost Intelligence for Argo CD is an open-source extension that shows each application's cost in a UI tab, using the previous 24 hours of OpenCost data after each sync. It requires Argo CD 3.4 to 3.6 and OpenCost 1.121.1 or newer.

devops.title: Kubernetes Gave AI Agents a Place to Run, But Not a Way to Recover
devops.summary: Kubernetes can restore an AI agent's environment but cannot record which steps finished, so restarted agents may repeat actions such as payments. The author argues for durable execution that logs each step, citing Dapr's workflow engine as an option.

devops.title: 7 Production Habits We Learned at Wix. The Hard Way
devops.summary: A Wix engineering lead details seven habits for reliable production systems, learned from eight years of operating the editor server team. The list includes using the Five Whys method to find root causes, running post-mortems without blame, and conducting team-wide on-call handovers. He emphasizes leaving the system better than you found it by fixing one small thing per shift.

devops.title: Let your AI agents run code with strong isolation
devops.summary: AI agents now write and execute code no human reviews first. AWS Nitro Sandboxes now runs each AI agent and container in its own lightweight VM on the AWS Nitro System, the same hardware isolation that separates every EC2 instance. Safely run untrusted, LLM-generated code with strong isolation and near bare-metal performance. Learn how it works here .

devops.title: Astryx
devops.summary: Astryx is an open-source design system with over 150 accessible components. It grew inside Meta over eight years to power more than 13,000 apps. The system is built on React 19 and StyleX, with a CLI designed for both human developers and AI assistants.

devops.title: HA-MCP
devops.summary: HA-MCP lets users configure and automate Home Assistant with AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT. The recommended integration installs directly through HACS or the built-in Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026.11+, runs in-process, and works across all installation types.

devops.title: CloudNativePG becomes a CNCF Incubating Project
devops.summary: CloudNativePG has moved from CNCF Sandbox to Incubation. The operator runs highly available PostgreSQL on Kubernetes and manages pods directly rather than through StatefulSets, handling failover, rolling updates, backups, and point-in-time recovery.

devops.title: MCP Server Security Holes & How to Plug Them
devops.summary: Model Context Protocol servers lack built-in authentication, rate limiting, and tool controls, creating security gaps for organizations. This guide explains how to deploy an AI Gateway to add token-based authentication and restrict which specific tools are available to users and agents.

devops.title: Give developers a security tool they'll actually use
devops.summary: Why choose between speed and security? 1Password secures developer secrets and AI-agent credentials at human and machine speed. Learn More.

devops.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
devops.summary: Entire, a Git forge led by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, is built for collaboration between developers and AI coding agents.

devops.title: Authenticate external gRPC clients with Amazon VPC Lattice
devops.summary: An Application Load Balancer validates external clients' JWTs, then an ECS proxy signs requests to private gRPC services with AWS SigV4.

devops.title: Running Kubernetes at Its Extremes
devops.summary: Kubernetes documents limits of 5,000 nodes and 110 pods per node, and its default etcd storage limit is 2 GB.

design.title: Adobe and Disney Team Up to Build AI Tools for the Next Generation of Storytelling
design.summary: Adobe has become Disney's Official AI Innovation Partner under a multi-year deal focused on storytelling, creativity, and responsible AI use. Adobe will give Disney early access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, and Photoshop, plus its own engineers and researchers. Through Firefly Foundry, Disney's models learn its characters and art styles, and Imagineering R&D already uses them to turn sketches into 2D concept art.

design.title: Instagram's Effect Builder Makes New Filters from AI Prompts
design.summary: Instagram's new Effect Builder, available now on the web to US residents over 18, turns AI prompts into custom Stories filters. Users can attach style reference images, preview effects on their own photos, and refine through follow-up prompts. An AI prompt-rewrite option adds paragraphs of style detail yet barely changes the result, and every effect must pass a safety review before others can use it.

design.title: Google Messages homepage redesign: Pinned chat avatars, bottom search, corner Gemini
design.summary: Google Messages is testing a redesigned Android homepage that displays pinned conversations as large contact avatars above the regular message list, similar to Apple's iMessage. Search moves from the top of the screen to a floating button near the bottom, alongside a new-chat button that changes shape while scrolling to improve one-handed usability. The Gemini shortcut also moves to the upper-right corner beside the profile image, with the changes currently rolling out selectively to beta testers.

design.title: When touch makes sense on a laptop
design.summary: Touchscreen laptops can make certain interactions faster than using a trackpad, particularly when selecting large targets or performing brief, direct actions. In a single-participant experiment across six tasks, touch averaged 1.39 seconds compared with 1.74 seconds for the trackpad, while previous research found similar advantages for some interactions. Touch remains less accurate for small targets and can cause fatigue during extended use, making it better suited as a complementary input method rather than a replacement for traditional laptop controls.

design.title: Making Immersive LLM Chat Experiences More Accessible
design.summary: Chat interfaces like Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini are interactive web content, so WCAG applies to them like any other page. A single live region announcing replies after streaming ends, hidden per-message headings, and sparing landmark use keep screen reader navigation workable. Skip links, Control+F6 shortcuts, user preferences, and research with disabled participants round out the approach.

design.title: Welcome to the Beige Era of Product Design. Here's Your Way Out
design.summary: Digital products are converging on the same look, driven by AI tools that repeat common solutions, vibe-design tools, shared UI libraries like shadcn/ui, and optimization culture. Convergence is "the floor," so designers should standardize what users expect. Borrowing automotive design's idea of "jewelry," teams should protect a few distinctive details, such as emotional moments like a first payment or a signed contract.

design.title: Publish Everywhere from One Place
design.summary: Choose a template, apply your style, and publish to your site, newsletter, and social — all in one workspace.

design.title: WCAG-EM Report Tool
design.summary: The WCAG-EM Report Tool turns your accessibility evaluation findings into a report.

design.title: AI Skills for Building Better Interfaces
design.summary: Emil Kowalski's collection of 17 AI agent skills helps developers build and refine interfaces through specialized guidance for animation, gestures, mobile interactions, prototyping, performance, accessibility-related edge cases, and design engineering.

design.title: "x is dead" is dead
design.summary: Figma, wireframing, design files, and design systems aren't disappearing, but the standardized toolchains that once defined product design are fragmenting into increasingly personalized workflows. Designers now move between sketching tools, AI prompts, coding agents, and other applications, making it harder for organizations to enforce consistency through shared software alone. Design systems must therefore become tool-independent infrastructure that communicates not just components and tokens but also product principles, decision-making context, and the intentions behind design choices.

design.title: The Relationship between Visual Design and User Experience Design
design.summary: Visual design is only one part of UX, usually among the last decisions made, and it depends on an interdisciplinary team. Jesse James Garrett's five planes run from strategy through scope, structure, and skeleton to surface, where visual design sits. Continuous testing feeds back into decisions at every level.

design.title: The "Ruined" GTA VI Ad Controversy Is Pretty Ironic
design.summary: Graffiti artist Jelous tagged the hand-painted GTA VI mural in Brooklyn, splitting opinions less than two weeks before the game's November 19 release.

marketing.title: About a Third of Americans Have Left an Online Community
marketing.summary: About one-third of adults in the US have left an online community. These include groups where people connect or participate together through social media, forums, messaging, or online games. More than 80% cite losing interest as a reason, while 57% point to too much arguing and 43% to harassment. Other reasons include excessive political discussions (40%) and spending too much time online (37%). Younger adults are more likely to leave, with 44% of those under 30 having exited a community compared with 19% of adults 65 and older.

marketing.title: ChatGPT just became the new Google Business Profile, and CMOs finally get the numbers
marketing.summary: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, giving brands verified profiles to update company information and track mentions, profile views, and website clicks. The dashboard offers the first official data on ChatGPT visibility but doesn't reveal the prompts driving mentions. Like Google Business Profile, it could become a standard business listing with ads built in. The launch also introduces Business Agents that let shoppers ask questions and compare products inside ChatGPT.

marketing.title: 236 PR ideas for GTA VI's launch
marketing.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches in 9 days, which is an opportunity for non-gaming companies to earn press coverage. This post includes 236 PR ideas, grouped into 11 plays, with what each one looks like for GTA 6. Each idea is based on a real campaign that got a brand outside gaming into the press.

marketing.title: Go for a 70-20-10 split on LinkedIn
marketing.summary: Grow your LinkedIn following with a 70-20-10 content split across roughly 20 monthly posts. Spend 70% (14 posts) on top-of-funnel content like industry news, humor, and relatable topics to reach a broader audience. Use 20% (4 posts) for tactical playbooks that solve specific audience problems. Reserve 10% (2 posts) for social proof, client wins, and promotional offers. Maximize reach and follower growth over lead generation, with optional weekend posts or experimental content to build familiarity.

marketing.title: Unboring Your Videos in Seconds with Mochine
marketing.summary: Have you got talking-head videos that aren't speaking to anyone? Demo clips that should have been demolished? Wistia's Mochine is the AI video editor that transforms the unwatchable into the unbeatable. Simply drop in one or more videos, pick a Motion Kit, and Mochine edits, animates, and makes it look terrific. Try Mochine for free.

marketing.title: PostSnag
marketing.summary: PostSnag is a Chrome extension and content research tool designed to automatically capture, organize, and analyze viral Facebook posts. It saves posts, Reels, and content from any Facebook profile, business page, or group as you scroll normally. It then sorts and ranks collected posts by likes, comments, shares, video plays, and post times. It's free to install and offers paid plans with additional features.

marketing.title: ChatGPT Is Now Showing Ads While Images Are Being Generated
marketing.summary: For free ChatGPT users, image generation now comes with ads attached. Labeled, multi-image units run while a picture renders for US users on the Free and Go plans. They fill the seconds a user already spends waiting for the picture, so the ad interrupts nothing. Free users can opt out of ads, but only by giving up image generation.

marketing.title: Before You Spend More on Ads, Find Out What Happened to Your Last 300 Leads
marketing.summary: Reviewing recent leads shows where the process breaks before more money goes into ads. If cost per lead is rising, the campaigns themselves likely need work. If many leads were never contacted, the problem is sales capacity, and more ads would only lengthen the queue. If leads were contacted quickly but rarely qualified, the problem is likely the offer, targeting, or form questions.

marketing.title: How software buyers use AI
marketing.summary: AI is introducing new software vendors to buyers who already have a shortlist. Wynter's survey found that 63% of buyers with existing vendor candidates added another option through AI. Buyers then use follow-up prompts to compare vendors and evaluate pricing, integrations, setup, and product fit. After using AI, 73% visited vendor websites and 48% used Google to continue their research. Marketers need to build brand awareness before buyers start searching and make sure their products appear in AI recommendations across multiple platforms.

marketing.title: We just got rid of titles at beehiiv
marketing.summary: beehiiv eliminated job titles to reduce internal bureaucracy and keep employees focused on customers rather than hierarchy. Managing titles created unnecessary work around leveling, promotions, and pay negotiations. These discussions led to meetings and internal politics without improving the product. Instead, employees are now identified by their job family, with “Lead” added for people managers. The company argues that growth should be measured through greater responsibilities and contributions rather than titles or rank.

marketing.title: Creators quit pro-AI platforms
marketing.summary: 75% of creators' posts about AI on these platforms are negative, driven by fears of having their work replaced or used for training without consent.

marketing.title: Google's Holiday 100
marketing.summary: 100 of the year's trending products wrapped by Google Trends.

marketing.title: Stop publishing new SEO content
marketing.summary: Prioritize updating existing pages ranking in positions 4-20 before creating new SEO content.

founders.title: Watch AI and SaaS pricing leaders at Monetize 2026
founders.summary: Watch four talks on pricing AI products and introducing usage-based models. Leaders from Replit, Fin, Snowflake, Clay, and Growth Unhinged discuss what to meter, how to show customers their variable spending, when to revisit a pricing model, and how to forecast AI costs and returns. Recorded at Monetize 2026 , Stripe and Metronome's conference on modern pricing and billing. Watch now .

founders.title: Inside the AI-Native Services Business Model
founders.summary: AI-native services companies promise the same quality as services businesses but with faster turnaround and typically at a lower cost. The market is big - arguably bigger than the software market. The challenge is in delivering more work without needing proportionally more people while maintaining quality and keeping enough of the efficiency gains. AI-native services may be reasonably easy to get off the ground, but scaling them is another story.

founders.title: The era of fully autonomous companies
founders.summary: We are now entering the era of autonomous companies. An autonomous company is a company managed entirely by agents. All management decisions are made by AI - there may be humans involved on occasion, but only at the very bottom of the hierarchy for specific tasks. By this time next year, there will be millions of autonomous companies, and many of them will be profitable.

founders.title: The Forward Deployed Engineer Your GTM Team Needs
founders.summary: Forward-deployed engineers embed with sales teams to identify manual handoffs, build CRM automations, train reps, and transfer ownership. This guide recommends prioritizing workflows by hours lost, retaining human approval for outreach, and measuring adoption, production workflows, time saved, and operation without external help.

founders.title: You're Hiring Too Many Reps
founders.summary: Lassie's revenue lead described $15,000-$20,000 annual contracts closing in six to seven days with a couple of calls and no solutions engineer. For your last ten closed deals, divide each deal's annual contract value by the human hours spent winning it, including sales engineering and legal work. If that number falls as you add reps, fix pricing and packaging before hiring more.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Build more efficient financial operations on the same platform your business already uses for payments as you continue growing. See how it works

founders.title: Cursor Projects is now multiplayer
founders.summary: Cursor Projects lets teammates work alongside AI agents in a shared workspace with common documents, decisions, and a task board. Agents can coordinate overlapping work and carry context across handovers instead of each teammate rebuilding it. The feature is rolling out in beta to all Cursor users starting November 10.

founders.title: ChatGPT visual ads are rolling out
founders.summary: OpenAI is rolling out visual ads in ChatGPT. Some users will now see ads when ChatGPT generates images. The ads disappear after the images are generated. A video that shows what an ad looks like is available in the article.

founders.title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
founders.summary: Businesses in ChatGPT gives businesses a new way to connect with ChatGPT users. Businesses can claim their businesses through Business Hub and see insights on how people engage with them on ChatGPT. OpenAI's Business Agents allow eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US to interact with users and help them explore products and services using the most accurate and up-to-date details. Users' conversations and Business Agent chats are not shared with businesses.

founders.title: Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors
founders.summary: Claude lets teams build spreadsheets together, organize data, edit formulas across multiple tabs, and map out ideas on shared whiteboards. Teams can turn a whiteboard discussion into a spreadsheet or dashboard without repeating the context, making it useful for account trackers, project updates, and planning. Interactive connectors bring apps such as Adobe and Atlassian directly into Claude, so teams can work with connected apps without switching tabs.

founders.title: Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend
founders.summary: Resend's pricing page uses an interactive slider for people, while adding .md to its URL gives coding agents the same prices as a Markdown table in one request. That lets an agent move from comparing providers to writing the integration. Check whether the version of your pricing page an agent reads returns a price for a specific volume.

founders.title: AI Startups May Have Fewer Sales Reps. But Not as a Percent of the Team. Has The Playbook Really Changed All That Much?
founders.summary: AI startups maintain a similar sales percentage, with 18.4% of their workforce in sales compared to 20.7% in traditional tech, despite smaller overall teams. Customer support shrinks drastically to 1.8% as AI handles repetitive tasks, while engineering expands to 47% due to the need for constant model updates and customer-specific configurations. These startups show higher output per sales rep and rely heavily on AI in sales development roles, but still require human sales teams for large deals.

crypto.title: MARA posts $634 million Q3 net profit on bitcoin gains
crypto.summary: MARA Holdings posted Q3 net profit of $634.4 million, up from $123.1 million a year earlier, as nearly $885 million in fair-value gains on digital assets offset a 37% drop in mining revenue driven by the April halving, pushing total revenue down 35% year-over-year to $164.2 million. After quarter-end, the company sold 13,597 BTC for roughly $1.1 billion, using $750 million to fully retire its bitcoin-collateralized loans and cutting total debt 37% year-to-date to $1.4 billion. MARA slipped to fifth among corporate bitcoin treasuries after Strive passed it, and is redirecting from infrastructure expansion toward securing customer leases, free cash flow generation, and AI/high-performance computing. CEO Fred Thiel framed the shift as moving from asset accumulation to execution discipline.

crypto.title: Elizabeth Warren to scrutinize prediction markets and Trump Crypto
crypto.summary: Elizabeth Warren will take the Senate Banking gavel in January after Democrats win the Senate, with priorities of affordability, AI, prediction markets, a looming financial crisis, and accountability. An aide says Trump family crypto businesses and others should “preserve their documents.” She has pressed Kalshi and Polymarket on insider trading and election bets, and has sought probes into Trump's memecoin and World Liberty Financial's UAE ties.

crypto.title: NYSE Selects Avalanche as Blockchain for Tokenized US Stock Settlement
crypto.summary: The New York Stock Exchange selected Avalanche as the exclusive settlement blockchain for a new 24/7 tokenized US equities trading platform. NYSE cited Avalanche's transaction speed, throughput, and compliance capabilities as key selection criteria. The platform targets a Q4 launch pending regulatory approval, and will offer instant settlement with stablecoin-based funding. The selection places AVAX at the core of NYSE's equity tokenization infrastructure, marking a direct integration between the US' largest stock exchange and a public layer-1 network for securities settlement.

crypto.title: Securitize pushes into asset-backed finance with River One acquisition
crypto.summary: Securitize agreed to acquire River One, a New York institutional financing firm backed by Framework Ventures and Maple Finance, to extend its tokenization platform into the $6.1 trillion asset-backed finance market. The deal adds warehouse financing capabilities, allowing clients to borrow against pooled loans ahead of refinancing, as the ABF market is projected to exceed $9 trillion by 2029 per KKR. Q3 results released alongside the announcement showed revenue of $18.6 million (+13% YoY), average tokenized assets of $5 billion (+39%), and transaction volume of $4.3 billion (+20%), with $300 million in cash and no debt on the balance sheet. The acquisition moves Securitize beyond fund and equity tokenization into private credit's largest sub-segment, deepening its utility for institutional clients including BlackRock, Apollo, KKR, Hamilton Lane, and VanEck.

crypto.title: ETH as Store of Value: Why Vitalik Is Shifting the Narrative
crypto.summary: Vitalik Buterin contends that ETH's value proposition is better grounded in store-of-value than in fee-burning mechanics, arguing that optimizing for burn would require trade-offs that undermine decentralization and capture resistance. EIP-1559's burn mechanism stays intact, but Buterin treats it as incidental, stating fee burn below 10% of breakeven is acceptable long-term since ETH's value comes from elsewhere. The SoV case rests on Ethereum's CROPS properties, which produce protocol-level stability, the attribute users placing assets in the network value most. Buterin cites the AI disruption era as the demand context where protocol-level stability becomes a concrete SoV advantage for ETH.

crypto.title: Your payment processor has a payment processor
crypto.summary: This article examines the terms of three merchants of record (Whop, Commas, and Dodo Payments) after seeing merchants report frozen funds and shut accounts. None explicitly names the processor or acquiring bank, so a decision made several layers up can freeze a merchant who has no direct relationship with the decision-maker. Terms allow holds of 180 days or longer, Whop reserves up to 100% for up to 180 days, and Commas calls some risk decisions final. Other sellers' fraud or disputes can also tighten rules for everyone on the platform. Although the MoR model works and saves real compliance work, the label covers different arrangements, so merchants should ask who processes payments, how risk is assessed, what the reserve terms are, who can release funds, and plan for a long hold.

crypto.title: OpenFX payment volume grew from $1B to $100B annualized in 2 years
crypto.summary: OpenFX CEO Prabhakar Reddy says the company started by converting currencies and delivering funds in under an hour, 24/7. After seeing customers park money with it overnight, it launched Global Accounts and Send in October so customers can hold funds and pay anyone in its markets. He says revenue grew faster than volume despite lower prices, and that licenses in the US, EU, UK, Canada, and UAE took two years. He expects cross-border settlement to consolidate into one or two companies, wants to be one of them, and hints at credit as a third layer. The company has nearly 200 staff and is hiring.

crypto.title: The House of Avalanche: chains, funds, cards, deeds, and clearing
crypto.summary: Chain INK frames Avalanche as five layers. Consensus saw Helicon cut block verification to 2ms in September. There are 71 active L1s, including Evergreen, Spruce, Dinari, and FIFA. BlackRock's BUIDL reached $486.5M on Avalanche in Q3, with Apollo, Franklin, and Janus Henderson also onchain. Payments include Wyoming's FRNT stable token, the Avalanche Card (record $10M Q3 spend), and Bergen County property deeds. On November 9, NYSE picked Avalanche for tokenized stock clearing, pending approval. The opening line notes Schwab listing SOL and LINK as well. Pro-AVAX framing, with figures unverified.

it.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available in AWS Marketplace
it.summary: OpenAI has made ChatGPT Enterprise available through the AWS Marketplace, allowing organizations to purchase and manage the AI product using their existing AWS accounts and billing relationships. Customers gain access to the same models and features available directly from OpenAI while being able to apply eligible spend toward AWS commitments. Additionally, eligible customers can access specialized offerings such as ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Financial Services.

it.title: Microsoft presses Trump to scuttle ban on Chinese data center tech
it.summary: Microsoft and industry groups are lobbying against a proposed US ban on new Chinese optical transceivers used in data centers. They warn that alternative suppliers lack capacity to replace Chinese vendors, potentially delaying construction and leaving purchased AI chips idle. The restrictions are still under consideration.

it.title: IT leaders seek alternatives for SAP, VMware, and Java
it.summary: Licensing increases and support deadlines are prompting IT leaders to explore replacements for SAP, VMware, and Oracle Java. Executives warn that integrations, training, disruption, and parallel operations can outweigh license savings. They recommend pricing a realistic exit before negotiations and distinguishing dissatisfaction from a workable migration plan.

it.title: Panic over cloud capacity is out of hand
it.summary: Claims that AWS and other cloud providers have sold out of AI capacity through 2027 exaggerate infrastructure shortages and create unnecessary concern for enterprises. While GPU, power, and infrastructure constraints affect large-scale AI training, standard inference and fine-tuning workloads remain feasible. Enterprises should distinguish between workload types, verify capacity directly with cloud providers, and build flexible architectures rather than react to market hype.

it.title: Expanding Gemini in Gmail to more Google Workspace users
it.summary: Google is expanding email-thread summaries and non-personalized Help me write to all Workspace users aged 18 or older with Gmail smart features enabled. These features are on by default, with user and admin controls to disable them. Rollout began on November 10 and could take up to 15 days.

it.title: Apptio Expands Portfolio to Help Enterprises Connect AI Spending to Business Value
it.summary: IBM expanded Apptio's AI spending tools and Kubecost's Kubernetes network-cost reporting. Available capabilities include AI usage connectors, financial planning for AI services, and more detailed AWS NAT Gateway, cross-zone, and cross-region cost visibility. The announcement also covers planned MCP servers and scenario-planning features, so availability varies across the portfolio.

it.title: Use Docker Sandboxes as Your Development Environment
it.summary: Docker Sandboxes provide isolated microVM-based development environments for building software projects, such as books using Pandoc and XeLaTeX, without cluttering the host system. Developers can use the sbx CLI to create sandboxes, configure network policies, and install necessary toolchains and dependencies. They can also preserve and reproduce these environments through snapshots or declarative Dockerfiles.

it.title: Royal Australasian College of Surgeons targets AU$2.1 million in savings with HPE Private Cloud
it.summary: HPE says RACS lowered its virtualization licensing bill by as much as 70% and reduced its fleet from eight servers to four. The migration followed a renewal quote that was roughly 300% higher. RACS projects a total AU$2.1 million benefit over five years, including planned infrastructure and disaster recovery improvements.
